We got a list of templates. Need to find one that matches our target molecule and corresponds to cycloaddition where ketone and C-C triple bond are lost. The first entry reaction_id 1914386 seems promising: It shows a mapped reaction where product is our target? Let's examine product_smiles: '[CH3:1][O:2][C:3](=[O:4])[C:5]1(/[CH:6]=[CH:7]/[c:8]2[cH:9][cH:10][cH:11][cH:12][cH:13]2)[CH:14]=[C:15]1[Si:16]([CH3:17])([CH3:18])[CH3:19]'

That matches our target: COC(C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/C2=CC=CC=C2)=O. Yes product is methyl ester? Actually COC(=O) ... The SMILES: COC(C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/C2=CC=CC=C2)=O. That's methyl ester of something. The product SMILES matches: CH3-O-C(=O)-C1(=... ) etc. So template 1914386 seems correct.

We need to return mapped_rxn and template_id (the one used to search the database not the hash). The template_id likely is reaction_id? Or template_id is integer identifier used to search. In search results, each entry has 'reaction_id' and 'template_hash'. The template_id likely is reaction_id. We'll assume template_id = 1914386.

We need mapped_rxn string from that entry: It's given as 'mapped_rxn': '[CH:14]#[C:15][Si:16]([CH3:17])([CH3:18])[CH3:19].O=[C:5]([C:3]([O:2][CH3:1])=[O:4])[CH2:6][CH2:7][c:8]1[cH:9][cH:10][cH:11][cH:12][cH:13]1>>[CH3:1][O:2][C:3](=[O:4])[C:5]1(/[CH:6]=[CH:7]/[c:8]2[cH:9][cH:10][cH:11][cH:12][cH:13]2)[CH:14]=[C:15]1[Si:16]([CH3:17])([CH3:18])[CH3:19]'

Check that matches forward? This is retrosynthetic direction? The mapped_rxn shows reactants (left) are alkyne with Si and ester chain, product is target. That's forward? Actually retrosynthetic template would be reverse: product -> precursors. But mapped_rxn is forward? It shows reactants -> product. That's fine; we just need to return mapped_rxn as given.

Thus final answer dict.
